data.name: Khalees
data.gender_notes: Khalees is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word 'Khali', meaning 'to be strong, powerful and brave'. The name Khalees carries the meaning “Mighty, Strong, Brave” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Khalees usually hope their child will grow to embody mighty, strong, brave and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes courage and strength, inspiring the bearer to overcome challenges and face adversity with fortitude.
data.etymology: Khalees belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Mighty, Strong, Brave.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Khalees total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Khalees" is an Arabic name with rich cultural significance. It is a name that signifies strength, courage, and power. In many Islamic communities, the name is associated with warriors and leaders. It is a name that inspires confidence, respect, and admiration.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name "Khalees" is a reminder of the strength and power that comes from within. It is a reminder that we all have the potential to be strong and brave, even in the face of adversity. The name reminds us to draw on our inner resources and to be confident in our ability to overcome challenges. It also serves as a reminder of the importance of courage and bravery in our spiritual journey. Ultimately, the name "Khalees" is a call to be strong in faith, to stand up for what is right, and to be a source of inspiration and guidance for others.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Kathir, Al-Bidayah wa-l-Nihayah, Vol. 7, p. 205 The name Khalees carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Mention of Khalees ibn Mughith al-Kilabi, a companion of Salahuddin Ayoubi, who led the army and took control of the fortress of Safed (in modern-day Israel) after Salahuddin's death.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Abi Dunya, Al-Amaali, Vol. 1, p. 117 The name Khalees carried significant weight in that era.
